text:
B: Hiya! Lorraine, is it? The other Lorraine, sorry, there's two of you.
A: That's me. The Wrexham one. Hiya.
B: Craig, Lancaster. Have you had a busy day of it?
A: Oh, that's my line. Erm, it's been alright. Lots of talking. I don't know if I've done it right.
B: There's no right, I don't think. I've just been chatting. Wrexham, though, that's exciting, isn't it, with the football.
A: Everyone says that. It's lovely for the town. You can't park, mind. Do you follow it?
B: Preston North End, unfortunately. I go with my dad. We drew again last week, it's what we do.
A: Oh dear.
B: Yeah. Weary affection, that's the phrase. What are you up to, are you working?
A: Not at the minute. I ran the morning cleaning team at the college. Took redundancy when the contract went. I'm after something part-time, but not supervising again.
B: No? Why's that, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Erm, it's the piggy in the middle bit. The staff are on at you one side, and the new contractor's on at you with targets the other side, and you can't make either of them happy. I liked the people. I'd cover their shifts, remember birthdays, show new starters how to do it proper. It was the spreadsheets and the being shouted at from above that got me. Sorry, I'm waffling.
B: No, honestly, you're not, mate. Sorry, not mate. But that's my whole job. I manage a bike shop, four staff. Owner wants the numbers, lads want Saturdays off. I'm on the rota every Sunday night going, someone's going to hate me.
A: You've got to do it with a cup of tea, the rota. That's the only way.
B: Cup of tea and biscuits. Noted. I thought you looked organised, in your picture. With the calendar on the cupboard.
A: That's from the Chinese takeaway! It's mostly the bin days on it. They've gone three-weekly now, I've had to write it all in.
B: Three-weekly? That's grim.
A: It is in summer.
B: I saw a kid's drawing on your fridge as well.
A: My grandson. He's five. It's a dinosaur, apparently. I'd not have known.
B: Ha. Do you get out much? Walking or anything?
A: Most days. My knee doesn't like the hills, but I go.
B: My knees are wrecked from five-a-side. I'm thirty-three, I sound like I'm ninety getting off the settee.
A: You want to rest them, love.
B: I won't, though. Sunday I'll be out on the bike up the Trough, and then a bacon barm after.
A: A what?
B: Oh no. Don't tell me. Bap?
A: Well, it's a bap. I have one from the café on market day.
B: That's three of you now. I'm outnumbered. I'm going to have to —
